edges.mechanism: Supplemental creatine is converted non-enzymatically to creatinine, raising serum creatinine (MD +0.13-0.14 mg/dL) and lowering creatinine-based GFR (MD -10.75 mL/min) without change in Cr-EDTA measured GFR; creatine ethyl ester produces marked 'pseudo renal failure'.
edges.evidence: Three MAs of RCTs (2025-2026) plus case reports; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Cystatin C is not raised by creatine and is the recommended confirmatory marker (eGFRcr-cys or measured GFR) when creatinine is confounded by creatine supplements.
edges.evidence: RCT (cystatin C fell on ~10 g/d), NHANES analysis, case report and KDIGO-based guidance

edges.mechanism: Endogenous creatine synthesis (renal AGAT) declines in CKD; safety data in established CKD are sparse, and creatinine-based eGFR becomes uninterpretable during use, complicating monitoring.
edges.evidence: MA including CKD/hemodialysis subgroup showed no measured-GFR change; reviews advise caution; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Creatine (especially ethyl ester) raises serum creatinine and can mimic allograft dysfunction, prompting unnecessary biopsy.

No controlled interaction data; creatine is not nephrotoxic in healthy-volunteer RCTs, but AIN has been reported with multi-supplement use and creatinine-based monitoring of drug nephrotoxicity is confounded; use cystatin C.
edges.evidence: Case report, safety reviews; very low certainty

edges.with: tubular creatinine-secretion inhibitors (trimethoprim, cimetidine, dolutegravir, cobicistat)
edges.mechanism: These drugs raise serum creatinine via OCT2/MATE inhibition without true GFR change; added to creatine-derived creatinine, the combined rise may be misread as AKI.
edges.evidence: Pharmacology review plus creatine MA; interaction inferred

edges.mechanism: Chronic caffeine during creatine loading may blunt creatine's ergogenic effect in some studies (opposing effects on muscle relaxation time; additive GI distress); creatine loading does not impair acute caffeine benefit.
edges.evidence: Systematic review of 10 studies, narrative review, RCT; mixed, low certainty

edges.mechanism: Complementary mechanisms (PCr resynthesis vs carnosine buffering); NMA found no synergy beyond creatine alone, SR suggests modest added anaerobic benefit; stacks present in a rhabdomyolysis case after extreme exertion.
edges.evidence: NMA of 52 RCTs, SR of 7 RCTs, case report; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Creatine with exercise improved glycemic control (HbA1c -1.1%) via GLUT-4 translocation; possible additive glucose lowering with glucose-lowering drugs.
edges.evidence: Single 12-week RCT (n=25) and SR; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Additive glucose lowering possible; trial populations did not include insulin-treated patients.
Creatine 5 g/d augmentation produced faster and greater HAM-D improvement in women with MDD, possibly via restored brain bioenergetics.
edges.evidence: Single RCT (n=52) plus SR of 5 RCTs; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Hypomania/mania occurred in 2 of 17 creatine-treated participants in psychiatric RCTs; no benefit in bipolar depression augmentation.
edges.evidence: SR of RCTs; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: High-dose creatine worsened activities of daily living and increased muscle pain in McArdle disease; no strength benefit in metabolic myopathies.
Dialysis patients may be creatine-depleted; pre-dialysis creatine reduced dialysis-associated cramps by 60%; serum creatinine rose slightly.
edges.evidence: Small RCT (n=10) and review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Creatine suppresses guanidinoacetate synthesis but did not lower homocysteine alone; creatine plus folic acid lowered homocysteine similarly to folic acid alone (no additive effect).
edges.evidence: RCT (n=458); moderate certainty for no additive effect

edges.mechanism: Cooked meat contains creatinine (from creatine) that raises serum creatinine for hours and can misclassify CKD stage; compounds supplement-related creatinine rise; fast 12 h before testing.
